#123024. Forest birds get more warning about predators when many other bird species live nearby

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1406 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚠️ Warning 🌐 Earth ↗ Open Full Page

Forest birds get more warning about predators when many other bird species live nearby

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1406 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Earth

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • More bird species meant more alarm calls when a model hawk flew past, and recordings of more species drew bigger crowds of mobbing birds.
  • According to recent reports, when an owl demonstrates up in a forest during daylight hours, the small birds that see it make lots of noise.
  • Industry observers note that A new study of forest birds in eastern China found more of these interspecies callings in places with greater bird species diversity.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

More bird species meant more alarm calls when a model hawk flew past, and recordings of more species drew bigger crowds of mobbing birds.

According to recent reports, when an owl demonstrates up in a forest during daylight hours, the small birds that see it make lots of noise. They gather around the owl and chirp out their calls. Almost immediately, birds of other species hear the calls and come to join the outcry.

Industry observers note that A new study of forest birds in eastern China found more of these interspecies callings in places with greater bird species diversity. Joining forces allowed them to make more calls per minute, alerting everyone within earshot of the owl’s presence.

The result suggests that birds in forests that have fewer species may get less predator warnings, leaving them more vulnerable.

It has been revealed that two doctoral students, Agnishikhe Kumar and Jiahao Wu, are the study’s first authors. Both are at Xi’an Jiaotong-Liverpool University in Suzhou, China, and the University of Liverpool.

Kumar and Wu worked with Eben Goodale, the study’s senior author, and with colleagues at Zhejiang University and other institutions in China, France, and the United States. All of the fieldwork took place in forest reserves in China.

Over more than two years, the team worked in ten nature reserves spread along about 1,025 miles (1,650 kilometers) of eastern China, from tropical Hainan to temperate Shaanxi.

Birds make two different kinds of calls about predators. Alarm calls go out when a predator is moving and attacking, and they often send the birds in a flock scattering into thick vegetation.

Recent findings suggest that mobbing calls are for a predator that isn’t moving, like an owl in daylight. These calls draw other birds toward the caller, and the crowd harasses the predator and can drive it away.

To set off alarm calls, the researchers used a slingshot to fire an 8-inch (20-centimeter) plastic hawk into the air beside mixed flocks of several species.

For mobbing, they put out a painted foam model of a collared owlet, a small owl that can attack birds, and played recordings of its calls.

It has been revealed that each time, they recorded how many species called, how many calls came per minute, and how rapidly the first call came. They also measured the range of pitch the calls covered.

In an interview with Earth.com, Goodale credited his two students with the fieldwork. “Yeah, this was a ton of work,” he noted. By his count, the total was 1,277 experiments.

Sources indicate that before each owl test, the team counted the bird species at the site. Where they counted more species, more kinds of birds joined the mobbing and more individual birds took part.

The birds at those sites also called at a higher rate, and their calls covered a wider range of pitch.

Sources indicate that pitch range matters because birds respond most to calls of other species that sound like their own. A broader mix of calls should reach more kinds of listeners.

Recent findings suggest that on 41 islands in Thousand Island Lake, a reservoir in Zhejiang Province, the team saw a similar pattern. The number of bird species on those islands goes up with the size of the island.

It has been revealed that alarm calls were far rarer than mobbing calls. The plastic hawk set them off in 79 of 150 flocks.

According to recent reports, the flocks that called gave a median of four alarm calls a minute, compared with a median of 52 calls a minute in the owl tests. One highly social species, Huet’s fulvetta, made 60.2% of all the alarm calls.

A bird that calls while a hawk is near may put itself at risk. Goodale told Earth.com the team thought the pattern might not hold for alarm calls, reasoning that “after one species calls, everyone else should eavesdrop on that and remain quiet.”.

Instead, in flocks with more species, more kinds of birds gave alarm calls. The calls came at a higher rate and covered a wider range of pitch.

Recent findings suggest that “We think it may be because the initial information may not be reliable,” Goodale said. Other species may need to keep calling, he added, to stress the threat and make sure the warning reaches their own kind.

According to recent reports, in Sri Lanka, the authors wrote, the first bird to call in a flock is usually a babbler. That babbler often calls at any large or fast-moving bird, so the later calls of other species help mark a real attack.

The team found no significant link between a flock’s species count and how rapidly the first alarm call came.

In a recent development, the hawk and owl tests demonstrated how much calling went on. To learn whether birds of other species made use of it, the team ran an experiment at seven sites on the largest island in the lake.

Through two speakers, the researchers played the mobbing calls of one, two, four, or eight local species and recorded which birds responded. A recording of crickets, played to check that birds weren’t simply reacting to noise, drew no response.

Across 406 trials, recordings with more species drew more kinds of birds and more individuals. The birds that came made more calls, across a wider range of pitch. The increase leveled off as the number of species in the recording went up.

Recent findings suggest that birds of species that weren’t in the recording were also more likely to call within the first minute when the recording held more species. When the team counted all responding birds together, the first-minute pattern was too weak to rule out chance.

Industry observers note that huet’s fulvetta leads the mixed flocks in the region and often starts the mobbing. Goodale noted the team expected it to play an outsized role in spreading information.

The experiment highlighted little sign of that. The team compared recordings of four species with and without each of the eight birds, across five measures.

In only four of those 40 comparisons was the response stronger when a particular species was included, and the four involved four different species.

Industry observers note that all eight species drew relatively similar responses, Goodale said. “It seems birds are responding to the small acoustic differences between species and registering a higher response when they hear more species,” he added.

To test that idea, the team had built each recording two ways. In one version, every recording had 104 calls per minute, however many species were in it. In the other, each species called at its usual rate, so more species meant more calls.

Birds responded more to recordings with more species even when the number of calls stayed the same. The researchers took that as evidence that the variety of calls matters.

On most of the five measures, adding species had a stronger effect when the number of calls rose too. So the amount of calling appears to matter as well.

Goodale said the finding also applies in reverse. In areas with fewer animals because of habitat loss, hunting, or other causes, the animals that remain could be less informed.

It has been revealed that or they could come to rely more on collecting information themselves. When the information is about predators, he stated, that could come at great cost.

The authors compared their finding to earlier studies that tied species diversity to pollination, seed dispersal, and pest control, and wrote that it helps justify conservation.

The experiments recorded how birds called and gathered, so they can’t show whether birds in places with more species are caught by predators less often.

Only mobbing calls were tested with recordings, and only on a single island. Earlier experiments elsewhere, which mostly compared one species with two, found weak effects on communication or no difference in response.

The larger scale of this study partly explains its stronger result, the authors wrote.

It has been revealed that the same idea could apply to other information, such as where to find food or habitat, and to other animals. The researchers suggested that experiments with the chemical signals of insects and other invertebrates may be particularly useful.

The full study was published in the journal PLOS Biology.

“The bottom line is we need to understand the magnitude of this with respect to Chinese intelligence, possible chip diversion,” said Rep. John Moolenaar, R-Mich., seen above. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call file photo).

The resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang on Thursday did little to quell bipartisan demands from Congress for an accounting of potential national security fallout from his affair with an alleged Chinese spy and talk of adding tougher chip export controls to the annual defense authorization bill.

Huang admitted on Sunday to having an affair, and reports say that it was with Alice Huang, an executive at Singaporean tech company and Nvidia customer Megaspeed, whom the U.S. government believes spied for China, according to recent reports. The Upcoming York Times and Reuters reported he also had affairs with two Nvidia employees.

In a recent development, senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., told reporters Thursday that he supports the Senate investigating Huang’s potential influence on U.S. artificial intelligence and chip policy.

“I think that it would make sense because of the… nature of the association… and the governments and the national security interests we were talking about here,” Thune said, though he said he thought it would be “wrong” to make assumptions about how close Huang’s relationship with President Donald Trump has been.

Sources indicate that senate Minority Leader Charles E. Schumer, D-N.Y., echoed the need for lawmakers to delve into the scandal, saying in a post on X that “Congress must demand answers.”.

According to recent reports, “The Trump administration must also answer for what it did once it learned about Mr. Huang’s relationship with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset. Were government officials told not to investigate because of Trump’s relationship with Mr. Huang? What did Trump know when he personally invited Mr. Huang aboard Air Force One?” Schumer wrote, referring to the president having invited Huang to accompany him to China in May.

House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., remarked at a press conference that Reps. Gregory W. Meeks, D-N.Y., and Jim Himes, D-Conn., the ranking members of the Foreign Affairs and Intelligence committees, respectively, are leading Democrats’ efforts to “get to the bottom of what has happened.”.

Sources indicate that “We need a classified briefing made available to members of Congress as it relates to the Nvidia situation,” Jeffries said. “And to the extent that our national security has been compromised, the American people deserve answers, and we're going to work to make sure that happens.”.

The investigations look likely to begin before control of Congress changes hands in January.

In a recent development, rep. John Moolenaar, R-Mich., who chairs the House select China committee, told reporters that his panel, along with House Foreign Affairs and Intelligence, are in negotiations with Huang to find a date for his testimony before Congress.

Industry observers note that “The bottom line is we need to understand the magnitude of this with respect to Chinese intelligence, possible chip diversion,” Moolenaar noted. “What ways is Chinese intelligence influencing his perspective, his perspective influencing national security policy?”.

Industry observers note that last week, the chairs of the three committees sent a letter to Huang requesting that he appear at a joint closed-door briefing. Moolenaar mentioned that if Huang does not agree to a date, the committees will subpoena him.

Recent findings suggest that late Thursday, he joined with House Foreign Affairs Chairman Brian Mast, R-Fla., and House Intelligence Chairman Rick Crawford, R-Ark., in sending a latest letter to Huang seeking a closed-door transcribed interview on Dec. 1. They also wrote to Nvidia General Counsel Tim Teter seeking a similar interview on Dec. 2. Separately, Mast wrote to Jeffrey Kessler, the Commerce Department undersecretary for industry and security, seeking his appearance at a committee hearing on Dec. 3.

It has been revealed that moolenaar also said that Congress needs to understand what privileged information Chinese intelligence may have gained access to through Huang and how they may have tried to influence U.S. policy.

“We need to have strong safeguards when it comes to our technology and export controls,” Moolenaar said. “And [Huang has] been one of the strongest proponents for not having export controls. This shines a whole latest light on that discussion.”.

Also late Thursday, Senate Banking Chairman Tim Scott, R-S.C.,  sent a letter to Huang calling on him to appear at a Dec. 3 committee hearing and another letter to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to testify at a Dec. 10 hearing "regarding recent public reports about NVIDIA and the Department of Commerce's role that raises national security concerns.".

Recent findings suggest that A proposed manager’s amendment to the Senate's fiscal 2027 National Defense Authorization Act bill (S 4784) contains several possibilities for those safeguards, including requirements for chip security mechanisms that would allow for verification if semiconductors are diverted to countries of concern and a ban on exporting certain very powerful chips to those countries. The House NDAA does not contain similar language.

However, House Armed Services Chair Mike D. Rogers, D-Ala., is open to the restrictions. He told reporters Wednesday that he “would like to see” semiconductor export controls in the NDAA, but that the Huang scandal had not changed his position.

Democratic Caucus Vice Chair Ted Lieu, D-Calif., told reporters on Thursday that after reports that the federal government had been aware of Huang’s affair with the alleged spy, the administration should have shared the information with Congress.

“The administration needs to be investigated for hiding this information from Congress and the American people,” he said.

Lieu also suggested that Nvidia’s reported donation to the White House ballroom project influenced the Trump administration’s decision to allow the export of some powerful Nvidia chips to China.

It has been revealed that “There is no reason to do that. That hurts our national security, and we have an opportunity right now to fix that in the upcoming National Defense Authorization,” Lieu noted.

It has been revealed that mast said the Huang revelations could give fresh momentum to including chip export rules in the NDAA. He also said that his “directive” on the concern came “straight from the admin” and informed his objectives on the committee.

“Don't let chips be smuggled to China. Make sure that American companies get to buy them first,” Mast remarked. “Make sure that the machines that make them don't get sold to them, even though it's the Dutch that make the machines. Make sure that they can't access it remotely.”.

Mast’s committee has advanced many of those priorities, including some of the language included in the NDAA.

In March, the committee on a unanimous vote advanced legislation known as the Chip Security Act, which would require chip security mechanisms to verify that certain semiconductors subject to export controls aren’t diverted to countries of concern, including China and Iran.

The committee also advanced bills to require the Bureau of Industry and Security and the State Department to work with allied suppliers of semiconductor manufacturing equipment to implement export controls to prevent the equipment from going to countries of concern, and to require licenses for the export of certain powerful chips, including banning exporting certain chips to countries of concern.

Versions of all three bills are included in the Senate manager’s amendment to the NDAA.

The scandal has also led to calls for oversight of the Commerce Department, including Secretary Howard Lutnick, for its handling of export policy and actions around Huang.

Sen. Thom Tillis, R-N.C., told reporters Thursday that Lutnick and Nvidia should testify “before Democrats can set the narrative.”.

According to recent reports, “If there is some reasonable basis or some way to discount some of the reporting, the best way to do it is request a meeting with us and give us a briefing,” Tillis noted. “Because otherwise, you're going to get what you get in an oversight hearing in about six weeks.”.

Industry observers note that asked about oversight of the Commerce Department’s role in the Huang scandal, Sen. Ted Cruz, R-Texas, who chairs the Commerce Committee, said his panel “has engaged in vigorous oversight under Republican presidents and Democrat presidents and will continue to be [engaged in it].”.

It has been revealed that on Wednesday, prior to Huang’s resignation, Senate Banking ranking member Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., and Sen. Chris Coons, D-Del., sent a letter to Lutnick, Secretary of State Marco Rubio and White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller requesting that they “preserve all documents, communications, records, and other materials regarding the export of NVIDIA’s advanced AI chips to China or to entities that may divert such chips to China.”.

“This incident raises significant concerns about the federal government’s ability to effectively enforce our export controls and protect our national security,” the senators wrote.

Recent findings suggest that in a statement Thursday, Warren said that Huang’s resignation did not “absolve” him of the need to answer questions. She also called for the passage of stricter export controls, including the bill to ban the export of certain chips to China.

Recent findings suggest that sen. Michael Bennet, D-Colo., sent his own letter on Wednesday to Lutnick, Rubio, Attorney General Todd Blanche and Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton, requesting an update on the Justice Department’s investigation into Megaspeed for possibly diverting U.S. chips to China.

Savannah Behrmann, John M. Donnelly, Jacob Fulton and David Jordan contributed to this report.

Countries clash over fossil fuels as COP31 ends without a major climate deal

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • COP31 ended without a major climate agreement after countries clashed over fossil fuels, emissions cuts and climate funding.
  • Industry observers note that the final draft of the main agreement at this year’s UN climate summit had one glaring omission.
  • Recent findings suggest that COP31 ended on Sunday, November 22, in Antalya, Türkiye.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

COP31 ended without a major climate agreement after countries clashed over fossil fuels, emissions cuts and climate funding.

Industry observers note that the final draft of the main agreement at this year’s UN climate summit had one glaring omission. Nowhere in the document did the words fossil fuels appear.

Several countries rejected it for that reason.

Recent findings suggest that COP31 ended on Sunday, November 22, in Antalya, Türkiye. The talks lasted two weeks and then ran two more days. That made it the longest UN climate summit on record.

Governments still did not agree on the main text.

UN Secretary-General António Guterres called the outcome “deeply disappointing.”.

“There may be no consensus in the negotiating room. There is no ambiguity in the science,” Guterres remarked in a statement.

Recent findings suggest that murat Kurum, Türkiye’s environment minister, was the president of COP31. He had little good news at the end of the summit.

“I understand that there is no agreement on this text. For that reason, these decisions have not been adopted,” Kurum said.

According to recent reports, australia led the negotiations. For several days it worked with Türkiye on latest versions of the agreement. Both countries tried to find language that everyone could accept.

Industry observers note that some countries wanted a firm commitment to use less coal, oil and gas. Countries that sell fossil fuels abroad worried about what that would mean for their economies.

The proposed text said the world is heading for more than 2.7°F (1.5°C) of warming.

Under the Paris Agreement, governments agreed to hold warming well below 2°C above preindustrial levels and pursue efforts to limit it to 1.5°C.

The text also asked for more technology to remove carbon dioxide from the air. It remarked nothing about burning less fossil fuel in the first place.

The European Union would not accept an agreement that avoided the subject. The bloc described the omission as “unconscionable.”.

Sources indicate that panama had sent a letter to the summit presidency with its priorities. Its delegation said governments had a responsibility “not to negotiate the minimum threshold, but to act.”.

In the Marshall Islands, where much of the land lies just above sea level, the stakes are particularly high.

Industry observers note that accepting the deal, the country’s delegation remarked, would mean betraying its own people. It rejected what it called “false solutions” and pushed for a faster, adequately funded shift away from fossil fuels.

Speaking for the African Group, Ghana raised concerns about climate funding and financial assistance for countries suffering climate damage.

There was also the question of how to support workers and communities as fossil fuel industries decline.

That issue got “a single generic sentence,” according to Ghana.

Nevertheless, the African Group chose not to block the deal, acknowledging that the text reflected the views of many countries.

Saudi Arabia saw things differently. Speaking for the League of Arab States, it defended keeping carbon capture and storage in the agreement.

This technology traps carbon dioxide and stores it before it reaches the atmosphere.

Was this simply greenwashing? Saudi Arabia argued otherwise, pointing to scientific assessments that give carbon capture a role in limiting global warming.

In a recent development, pakistan urged countries to keep talking. Its delegation noted climate action needs “bridges, not barriers.”.

Part of the frustration at COP31 goes back three years.

Sources indicate that at the 2023 climate summit in Dubai, governments agreed to transition away from fossil fuels. Guterres mentioned countries now need to speed up that transition and pay for it.

“We can’t put out the fire while pouring fuel on it,” he mentioned.

Guterres also blamed powerful fossil fuel interests for holding back climate action while they keep making profits.

It has been revealed that he wants deeper emissions cuts before 2030. He also wants more money for vulnerable countries to cope with climate change.

Not everything fell apart in Antalya. Governments agreed on several smaller decisions.

Simon Stiell, the head of UN Climate Change, pointed to progress on the just transition.

In a recent development, picture a town where hundreds of families depend on a coal mine. When the mine closes, those families need help. A just transition means supporting workers and communities through changes like that.

Governments will continue their work on the matter for three more years. They will also set up a mechanism in stages. Intends for it were first agreed at last year’s summit in Belém, and formal adoption is expected at COP32.

Countries that make up about half of the world economy backed a goal of 35% electrification by 2035.

In practice, that means more cars, heating systems and factory machines running on electricity instead of burning fuel.

The International Energy Agency estimates the pledge could raise the global electrification rate from 23% to more than 33% by 2035.

Stiell noted progress like this could help bring about positive tipping points in climate action.

Tropical rainforests got some good news too. Pledges to the Tropical Forest Forever Facility, which helps protect these forests, reached $8.3 billion.

Stiell talked openly about what went wrong in Antalya in his closing remarks. “The world cannot afford a repeat of this moment,” he said.

He also spoke about how governments make decisions at these summits.

It has been revealed that “This process belongs to 194 Parties. Consensus works best from the ground up,” Stiell said.

In a recent development, next year, Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, will host the climate talks. Countries will pick up where they left off in Türkiye.

In a recent development, there is still no agreement on how quickly the world should move away from coal, oil and gas. For poorer nations, another problem remains: who will pay for the transition?

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that this is a human-written story voiced by AI. Got feedback? Take our survey . (See our AI policy here .).

Dor Minzer remembers sitting in an undergraduate computation class at Tel Aviv University. He was intrigued by his professor and soon found himself pulled into a latest world: the mystifying intersection of math and computation, first laid out by Alan Turing during World War II. Working with the professor, Minzer became deeply interested in the limitations of what computers can and can’t do.

Recent findings suggest that “My part is actually to prove not only do I not know how to do it, but I can prove that it’s impossible,” Minzer states. “You have to really be curious.”.

Minzer’s hard work has paid off. In 2018, he proved a theoretical computer science problem called the 2-to-2 games conjecture. It asks whether computers can efficiently distinguish games where almost all rules can be satisfied from those where almost none can be satisfied, when the rules have a strict structure.

It has been revealed that in September, Minzer and his two graduate students at MIT posted a 95-page milestone paper on the unique games conjecture, which builds off the 2-to-2 conjecture. The paper wasn’t quite ready, but they published to get ahead of a press release from OpenAI, describing its proof for the same problem, slated for only days later. It’s a situation that many mathematicians have found themselves in this year as AI companies flood the field with findings at lightning speed.

Minzer says it’s critical to remember that math, and all the research and contemplation behind it, is very human. “It’s a human activity,” he says. “Research is sort of a living organism, a living body.”.

According to recent reports, minzer teaches his own students now. Some days, he talks to his class and gets the sense that nobody is paying attention. But other days, he gets a few students that participate. They have ideas, they’re excited, and they remind him of his own days as a graduate student.

“I feel like now I feel like I’m passing the torch,” he claims. “Before you have a Ph.D. adviser, you’re like a latest person in a dark room. There are infinite places to go. Your Ph.D. adviser is the person that holds your hand and says, ‘Okay, let’s walk here.’”.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • EST, bringing us our second Super Moon of the year.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Looking for a sky event this week? Check out our full Sky This Week column.

November 23: Double star Kurhah in Cepheus.

Full Moon occurs at 9:54 A.M. EST, bringing us our second Super Moon of the year. A Super Moon occurs when the Moon reaches Full phase close to perigee, its closest point to Earth, making our satellite appear larger and brighter than average. The November Full Moon is also called the Beaver Moon.

A few hours earlier, before dawn, the Full Moon passes through the Pleiades star cluster (M45) in Taurus, occulting several of its bright stars. This is an easy event to watch, visible to the naked eye — or you can get a closer view with binoculars or a telescope (just note that you may want a Moon filter if available, as our satellite is so big and bright). The timing of the event will depend heavily on your location; note that it begins right around sunrise along the East Coast, so observers there may only see the Moon approaching the famous group of stars.

The 5th-magnitude star Celaeno (16 Tauri) disappears behind the Moon’s leading edge just moments before 6 A.M. CST, followed minutes later by 4th-magnitude Taygeta (19 Tau). Next to vanish is 4th-magnitude Maia (20 Tau) just before 6:20 A.M. CST, followed swiftly by Sterope (21 Tau) a few minutes later. The latter two may be difficult to catch from the Midwest without optical aid, as sunrise is fast approaching. If you are using binoculars or a telescope in this region, make sure to put them away several minutes ahead of sunrise from your location. Celaeno reappears around 6:40 A.M. CST, 15 minutes or so before sunrise.

For specific timings from your location, visit the International Occultation Timing Association at http://www.lunar-occultations.com/bobgraze/index.html.

According to recent reports, sunrise: 6:55 A.M.Sunset: 4:38 P.M.Moonrise: 4:24 P.M.Moonset: 7:10 A.M.Moon Phase: Waning gibbous (99%)*Times for sunrise, sunset, moonrise, and moonset are given in local time from 40° N 90° W. The Moon’s illumination is given at 10 P.M. local time from the same location.

Alison Klesman is senior editor of Astronomy magazine. She holds a Ph.D. in astronomy and has studied a variety of topics, from minor planets to supermassive black holes.

#123017. In 1935, crews dangled from cliffs to build a Grand Canyon phone line, now the Park Service wants to its copper wire

Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Earth ↗ Open Full Page

In 1935, crews dangled from cliffs to build a Grand Canyon phone line, now the Park Service wants to its copper wire

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (716 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Earth

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that hanging wires in the inner canyon put helicopter and emergency operations and wildlife at risk.
  • In the 1934-35 season, Civilian Conservation Corps crews built a telephone line down into the Grand Canyon and up the other side, according to a National Park Service history page.
  • It has been revealed that the line connected the North and South rims in 1935.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that hanging wires in the inner canyon put helicopter and emergency operations and wildlife at risk. The Park Service says removing some would be an adverse effect on a listed historic line.

In the 1934-35 season, Civilian Conservation Corps crews built a telephone line down into the Grand Canyon and up the other side, according to a National Park Service history page. Workers often had to dangle from ropes on the cliffs to set poles into the rock.

It has been revealed that the line connected the North and South rims in 1935. It gave the two rims instantaneous communication, though it could handle only one call at a time, according to the park.

More than 90 years later, the Park Service has proposed removing sections of the line’s wire. Its original copper wire, now hanging or lying in places across the inner canyon, has become a hazard for helicopter and emergency operations and for wildlife.

The Trans-Canyon Telephone Line runs through the inner canyon, generally following the Bright Angel and North Kaibab trails, with a spur toward the South Kaibab Trail.

Industry observers note that it was strung from tree to rock, the park says, and it was frequently out of commission. While the park’s history page says the CCC built the line, the agency’s newest notice describes it as “reconstructed by Civilian Conservation Corps crews in 1935.”.

It has been revealed that the Civilian Conservation Corps was created in 1933, when President Franklin Delano Roosevelt signed the law that set it up. The program gave poor, unemployed young men work on conservation projects across the country’s public lands.

Recent findings suggest that at the Grand Canyon, its crews built trails, walls and shelters, and they helped the park put in roads, campgrounds and telephone lines. The program ended in 1942.

Today the line is listed in the National Register of Historic Places for its importance to the park’s communications, engineering and administrative history.

Industry observers note that but according to the Park Service, suspended, hanging and fallen telephone wires have created risks to helicopter and emergency operations in the inner canyon. They can also pose entanglement hazards for wildlife.

In a recent development, under the proposal, the park would remove sections of the historic wire where necessary to eliminate those hazards. On the wire it keeps, it would add visibility markers where appropriate.

The historic poles, cross-arms, insulators and other hardware would stay in place, unless one of them presents a safety hazard of its own.

The plan is still a proposal, not finished work. The park took public comments for 15 days, from October 28 until midnight on November 11, 2026, and that comment period has now closed.

The Park Service acknowledges a cost to the historic line. Because the original copper wire is an key historic feature of the line, removing portions of it and adding markers “would alter characteristics that contribute to the property’s historical significance,” the agency remarked.

Under the National Historic Preservation Act, it added, “those changes are considered an adverse effect.”.

To deal with that, the park worked with Arizona’s State Historic Preservation Officer on a draft Memorandum of Agreement.

According to the Park Service, the agreement would let the park address known safety hazards while documenting and preserving the history and significance of the telephone line.

Sources indicate that the telephone line is one of many pieces of the Grand Canyon that date to that era. Hikers on the Bright Angel Trail still use resthouses built by the CCC, and Bright Angel Campground sits on the site of the corps’ camp at Phantom Ranch, the park notes.

Elsewhere in the park, the South Rim hotels reopened 81 days after a deadly flood, which echoed a disaster in 1966.

According to recent reports, the canyon’s rocks hold a far older record. Geologists have found fossils of unexpected creatures in the Grand Canyon’s Bright Angel Formation.

The information was obtained from the National Park Service news release Grand Canyon National Park Seeks Public Comment on Trans-Canyon Telephone Line (October 28, 2026) and the Grand Canyon National Park history pages Building the National Park and Civilian Conservation Corps.

Oceanfront structures in Rodanthe could collapse during a storm forecast for North Carolina’s Outer Banks on November 25 and 26, the Park Service warns

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (728 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Earth

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that damaged septic systems could expose waste on Rodanthe beaches, and drivers should avoid vulnerable parts of N.C.
  • Recent findings suggest that people on North Carolina’s Outer Banks should stay out of the ocean, avoid driving on the beach and avoid vulnerable sections of N.C.
  • A coastal storm is forecast to bring strong, gusty winds and elevated water levels to Cape Hatteras National Seashore on those two days.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that damaged septic systems could expose waste on Rodanthe beaches, and drivers should avoid vulnerable parts of N.C. Highway 12 at high tide.

Recent findings suggest that people on North Carolina’s Outer Banks should stay out of the ocean, avoid driving on the beach and avoid vulnerable sections of N.C. Highway 12 at high tide on November 25 and 26, according to the National Park Service.

A coastal storm is forecast to bring strong, gusty winds and elevated water levels to Cape Hatteras National Seashore on those two days.

In the village of Rodanthe, threatened oceanfront structures “could partially or completely collapse,” the Park Service warned on November 24.

It has been revealed that this is a warning, not a report of damage. But the seashore notes the risk goes beyond the structures themselves.

Damaged septic systems could expose waste, the Park Service stated, “creating serious hazards for people walking on the beach or wading nearby.”.

Most off-road vehicle routes on the beach will likely be impassable during the storm, according to the seashore, and hazardous surf will make swimming unsafe. Visitors should avoid beach driving and stay out of the water until conditions improve.

It has been revealed that N.C. Highway 12, the main road along the islands, is also at risk. The Park Service notes travelers should avoid its vulnerable sections during high tides on November 25 and 26, and that hazardous weather may cause road closures.

It lists four areas where driving may be very difficult during the storm:.

On Ocracoke Island, a two-mile stretch of highway south of off-road vehicle ramp 59.

On southern Hatteras Island, the road between the villages of Hatteras and Frisco.

On central Hatteras Island, the area along the northern boundary of Buxton.

On northern Hatteras Island, the road between the Pea Island Visitor Center and the Basnight Bridge, as well as side streets in northern Rodanthe.

All of the seashore’s campgrounds remain open, the Park Service says, but minor flooding and strong wind gusts will make for unfavorable camping conditions.

It points travelers to the National Weather Service at weather.gov/mhx for forecasts and to the North Carolina Department of Transportation at drivenc.gov for road conditions.

The seashore has issued similar warnings in 2026.

In a recent development, on April 7, it urged visitors to use caution on east-facing beaches through April 11. The potential for multi-day, persistent northeast winds and breaking waves, it noted, could cause coastal erosion and “the partial or full collapse of one or more threatened oceanfront structures in Buxton and Rodanthe.”.

At that time, the entire beach in front of Buxton was closed because of hazards from threatened oceanfront structures “in or near the ocean,” according to the Park Service.

Sources indicate that after a recent coastal storm, the seashore reported significant impacts in a September 28 upgrade. It said Dare County had declared a state of emergency for Hatteras Island, and non-resident travel to the island was prohibited.

According to recent reports, the Avon Fishing Pier had an estimated 20-foot gap in its structure. The beach was closed from the northern boundary of Rodanthe to the pier in Rodanthe, and people were told to avoid the ocean because of possible poor water quality from damaged septic systems.

Private beach stairs and boardwalk decking, septic system parts, and wooden and metal debris from houses were littering the beach, the Park Service remarked at the time.

Cape Hatteras National Seashore sits on barrier islands, and those islands are not fixed in place. One study predicts that barrier islands will retreat faster than they have in the past, and healthy dunes help protect the coasts behind them when storms hit.

The Park Service’s advice for now is practical: use caution on the beach, avoid beach driving and stay out of the water during the storm, and check road conditions before driving N.C. Highway 12.

The information was obtained from the National Park Service news releases Cape Hatteras National Seashore Warns of Hazardous Conditions and Threatened Structures During Coastal Storm (November 24, 2026), Cape Hatteras National Seashore Reports Status Updates After Recent Coastal Storm (September 28, 2026) and Cape Hatteras National Seashore Urges Caution Near Threatened Oceanfront Structures in Buxton and Rodanthe (April 7, 2026).

The 8 Best Solar Generators Provide Reliable Backup Power in a Pinch

📅 13 Aug 2021 | ⏱️ 17 min read (3469 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popularmechanics

⏱️ ~17 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Gear-obsessed editors choose every product we review.
  • Power stations (i.e., solar generators) have become increasingly popular because they are easy to run, cost less over time than gas generators, and offer eco-friendly, emission-free operation, especially when paired with a solar panel.
  • Unlike fuel-based generators, solar generators can’t create electricity in real time.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Gear-obsessed editors choose every product we review. We may earn commission if you buy from a link. Why Trust Us?

Power stations (i.e., solar generators) have become increasingly popular because they are easy to run, cost less over time than gas generators, and offer eco-friendly, emission-free operation, especially when paired with a solar panel. Some are small and compact, ideal for off-grid adventures, while larger ones are able to back up critical home circuits during a blackout.

Unlike fuel-based generators, solar generators can’t create electricity in real time. They’re giant battery packs, not true generators, and need to be recharged using alternating current (AC) power or solar panels, the latter of which often takes many hours in ideally sunny conditions.

Sources indicate that despite those distinctions compared to portable generators, there’s nothing more convenient than a power station for charging or running everything you need for day-to-day life—phones and laptops, lights, and even a small appliance or two. Plus, it’s nice to have a device that doesn’t produce carbon emissions and replenishes itself freely from the sun’s rays. Whether you’re seeking a highly portable option or need one that’s heavy-duty enough for extended use, these are the best solar generators we’ve tested and researched to date.

Sources indicate that to pick the best solar generators, we tested some of these power stations for charging capacity, ease of use, weight, and different use cases. Our picks were reviewed by Popular Mechanics editor Brad Ford, who provided input for the larger-capacity units. Other models on this list were reviewed by test editor David Dritsas or freelance writer Maggie Slepian.

Recent findings suggest that our primary concerns were portability and convenience. Ease of use was also notable—was the display easy to read? Did the screen readouts make sense? Bonus points if we could tell how much power is available at a glance. In the past few years, these criteria have become easier to meet. There are now plenty of compact, affordable units that have better charging capabilities than before.

Very few power stations of this size can handle as much solar input power as the Bluetti Apex 200. With two input types—low-voltage XT60 (up to 1,000 watts) and high-voltage MC4 (up to 2,000 watts)—it can accept up to 3,000 watts of solar power. If you had the panels and ideal weather, you could fully charge this station in less than 2 hours—even faster than plugging it into the wall. That’s impressive.

It has been revealed that it also balances nicely between being a portable station and a home backup solution. It offers 3,200 watts of continuous power (it says 3,600 on the front, but that’s only if it’s connected to an expansion battery). We were able to power a refrigerator for a full 27 hours on a single charge, and estimated the battery efficiency at 90 percent, which is very good. Meanwhile, the 2,560-watt-hour battery capacity is expandable by adding up to six additional batteries. Using Bluetti’s largest battery, the B500K, you could build a massive 33-kilowatt-hour system.

While 3,600 watts isn’t enough to power a whole home, you could power a couple of circuits through a manual transfer switch using the 120-volt 30-amp output. But keep in mind that there’s no 240-volt support, so you can’t use it to power high-voltage appliances like electric dryers.

As a portable station, the Apex 200 has a lot to offer. At 59 pounds, it’s not too hard to move around the house or in and out of a vehicle. And there are several great DC power options, including a bank of USB outlets (two are high-power USB-C) and both 10- and 30-amp, 12-volt outputs. We also love that the AC ports can individually be turned on and off using the mobile app; this helps improve overall runtime.

Since very few stations can match its max solar input capacity, we concluded that the Apex 200 is definitely a top choice for anyone who wants a power station that can recharge using the sun’s rays, but also offers the versatility of being used on the road or at home.

Full Bluetti Apex 200 Power Station Review.

This model replaces the original Jackery 1000, but many of the same observations made of the first model still apply. The new version has a slightly higher capacity of 1,070 watt-hours and uses a newer lithium iron phosphate (LiFePO4) battery, which is a newer battery technology that offers a longer lifespan (4,000 cycles versus 500 cycles for this model) and better performance in extreme temperatures.

Expert Maggie Slepian used the previous model on a media trip where she had to keep multiple camera batteries charged during a weeklong outing. She found that while the capacity was lower than you'll find with others on this list, it actually powers items for longer than some higher-capacity models. She also charged her photographer’s camera batteries while charging the power bank on solar power (it was a very sunny winter day), which proved effective and efficient.

Recent findings suggest that the newer V2 model has seven ports, including three AC outlets, two USB-C ports (one 30-watt and one 100-watt), a 12-volt car port, and one standard 18-watt USB-A outlet. It charges a typical laptop eight times or powers a small refrigerator or an electric cooler for over 15 hours.

In a recent development, the Jackery Explorer 1000 V2 charges with a 200-watt solar panel or a 12-volt outlet in your vehicle while you’re on the move. It has fairly standard charging times, with 11.5 hours in a car outlet, 6.5 hours for solar panels, and just 5.5 hours to fully charge in a wall outlet. This won’t be your best bet for powering larger appliances, but it’s an ideal power station for smaller items and off-grid camping.

According to recent reports, this power station takes solar recharging seriously. The Elite 300 can accept up to 1,200 watts of input, which is a high amount for a station this size. We paired it with a 250-watt portable panel and, on a fully sunny day, got around 260 watts of input. That’s the typical efficiency of a portable panel (again, you’ll never get 100 percent). But pair it with some larger panels, and you’ll get even more.

It also boasts an impressive battery capacity of just over 3,000 watt-hours and 2,400 watts of output, which is high for a station of this size. Plus, it includes a 120-volt 30-amp port, which is handy for connecting it to a small RV or pop-up camper, allowing you to run small appliances and water pumps. It’s not enough power to run a heating or cooling system for a significant amount of time, but for lights, small appliances, and other items that need power, this station will deliver.

If there’s one downside we found, it’s that there’s no way to add an expansion battery to increase your capacity. That’s not a huge detractor, but it’s something we’ve seen in stations even smaller than this one. But at the end of the day, the Bluetti Elite 300 solar generator offers the right balance between a midsize power station that delivers a lot of power and run time, and a station that is compact and portable enough to be perfectly suited for an outdoor adventure.

Full Bluetti Elite 300 Solar Generator Review.

The EcoFlow Delta Pro is a large portable power station with an output that rivals some gas portable generators. When sold in a bundle with solar panels, like the package with two 220-watt portable panels we tested, it becomes a powerful solar generator. With an output of 3,600 watts, the Delta Pro can charge multiple appliances, and the output has the ability to bump up to 4,500 watts with its built-in X-Boost technology if more power is needed.

In a recent development, to get an idea of the run time, we used the Delta Pro to power a full-size, 25-cubic-foot refrigerator—which it did for a remarkable 51 hours and 24 minutes. When recharged from a standard outlet, it took only two hours and 36 minutes. But it also charges with the included adapter, at electric vehicle charging stations, with a DC car adapter, or with the solar panels that come with the unit. Through the 30-amp connection, you can also connect this to a transfer switch to directly power select circuits in your home.

Industry observers note that like any power station with a large battery capacity, it will take a long time, perhaps nearly two days, to recharge this station using the bundled 220-watt solar panels. The good news is the Delta Pro accepts up to 1,600 watts of solar input, so it can charge faster by connecting more panels.

The heavy-duty wheels and telescoping handle on Anker’s Solix F3000 are easy to use, allow you to stand upright when pulling, and are a dream for people who regularly find themselves moving their power station around, whether it’s at a campsite or to different parts of the house during a power outage.

Along with convenience, this generator is a powerhouse with the capacity to easily run your refrigerator or a greenhouse heater, or keep your RV bright and warm.

It has been revealed that we were impressed with Anker’s app, which allows us to check the charging status or power being generated without continually going outside to check. The app also lets you turn the power to the AC and USB ports on and off remotely, keeping tabs on how much energy is being utilized.

It has been revealed that the Solix F3000 has 11 ports, including two car ports, an RV-specific outlet, four AC ports, three USB-C charging ports, and two USB-A. In sunny conditions and moderate temperatures, it recharges with a 400-watt solar panel in just a few hours and supports up to 2,400 watts of solar input.

According to recent reports, one of Jackery’s most recent solar generators is also its most rugged, able to withstand the elements better than most. It achieves this with an IP65 weatherproof rating, molded rubber port covers, a shockproof enclosure, and a bottom drainage system, which is part of a titanium alloy cooling structure that helps keep water out of the enclosure.

Sources indicate that we got a chance to see these features up close and were impressed by them all, as well as a very sturdy enclosure that, thanks to the cooling system design, eliminates any side vents that could allow water to get inside. It feels strong; you could bang this station around without worrying too much about damaging it. The only downside is that this denser construction adds a bit of weight.

In a recent development, as a power station, it delivers 1,800 watts of output with a battery capacity of 1,536 watt-hours. That’s enough power for a weekend camping trip or for running low-powered small appliances and some lighting during an emergency. As a solar generator, it can handle up to 800 watts of input from a portable panel. We paired it with a Jackery 200-watt panel, and it worked well. Overall, if your off-road adventures often get a little dirty, but you need some extra power, the Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra Power Station is a good one to have at your side.

Full Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra Power Station Review.

The latest version of the Goal Zero Yeti 1500 is a well-designed power station that’s ideal for off-grid camping situations where dust, wind, and potentially wet conditions are always on the table. This 2,000-watt power station is weatherproof with an IPX4 rating and features outlet shields that cover the ports and inputs. Each section is well-lit by an LED light that’s individually turned on or off using a manual button or the mobile app (and will shut off if not used after a certain period).

There’s a healthy number of outputs on the Yeti 1500, including four 120-volt AC outlets, four (two are high-powered) USB-A ports, and four 12-volt connections. We simulated an emergency blackout and managed to run a cable modem with a WiFi router, a lamp, a TV, and a tower fan, while charging a phone and a laptop through the USB-C ports. Given the station’s output and capacity, there was enough power for over two days of use (conveniently shown on the main display), and there was plenty of room to spare for a few more devices.

To test its solar capabilities, we paired the Yeti 1500 with a Nomad 200-watt portable solar panel and connected it using the high-voltage DC input, which accepts up to 600 watts; however, it also features a low-voltage input that accepts up to 300 watts for smaller panel arrays. Because both inputs can be used simultaneously, you could theoretically pair with two arrays for up to 900 watts, which is a high amount of input for a station of this size.

Recent findings suggest that of course, no portable panel operates at 100 percent efficiency. Even on a sunny, cloudless day with no shade-causing obstructions, the input readings demonstrated anywhere from 125 to 145 watts. After initiating a recharge with only 5 percent capacity left, it would take at least 10.5 hours in those conditions to recharge. That’s actually not bad. An average of about 70 percent efficiency for a portable panel is good.

Full Goal Zero Yeti 1500 Review.

Recent findings suggest that the Anker Solix C2000 power station can deliver the full 2,400 watts of output to the bank of five AC outlets—something similar stations don’t offer. This allows you to power several things at once, like a refrigerator, toaster, router, and chargers, all at the same time.

During our tests, we were able to take full advantage of this, powering a refrigerator (by itself for up to 18 hours), along with some high-powered appliances, like a four-slot toaster and an electric kettle (though not the last two at the same time).

Another interesting ability of the C2000 is that you can fast charge it from AC power up to 1,800 watts, but that recharging rate remains consistent if you’re powering other devices at the same time (we confirmed this with a wattmeter). For example, we ran a 1,400-watt space heater while still recharging at the full 1,800-watt rate. Other power stations offer similar fast charging but will throttle the amount of power coming into the station while powering devices.

Industry observers note that for solar recharging, we were a bit disappointed that this station can only accept 800 watts of input; other stations of this size accept more. But when solar was plugged in, it worked well. We connected it to a 200-watt Anker portable panel, and in full sun, we were getting around 125 to 145 watts of input, which is pretty good as these types of panels go. The C2000 is not IPX-rated for any type of weather resistance, however, so we would not recommend leaving this station sitting outside if the weather turns wet.

Full Anker Solix C2000 Power Station Review.

Recent findings suggest that power stations use watts and watt-hours to express size and capacity. Watts (size) refer to how much power it produces. For example, if you need to run a 900-watt microwave, you’ll need a station that outputs at least that much power (ideally more, since factory specs are never exact).

Meanwhile, watt-hours (capacity) give you an idea of how long devices can be powered continuously, though how much time depends on the amount of power being drawn—watt-hours don’t dictate a set time frame. Higher-powered devices will drain the battery a lot faster than lower-powered ones.

That may seem confusing, but a simple equation gives you an approximate idea of how it works: total watt-hours (of the generator) ÷ watts (of the device) = hours the power station runs.

Sources indicate that for example, if you had a power station with a 2,048-watt-hour capacity and wanted to run a 750-watt space heater consistently at its highest setting, it would probably run for around 2.5 hours, so long as nothing else is plugged in. But for a refrigerator, whose power draw fluctuates between 10 and 300 watts (depending on how often the compressor turns on), you might be able to run it for nearly 24 hours.

Keep in mind that manufacturer specs are taken from perfect conditions; in the real world, you’ll likely see slightly less capacity from your power station. If you’re not sure how much power the different devices in your home draw, sometimes it’s written on a label, or you can use a device like a wattmeter.

Just as a power station has specifications on output size and capacity, solar panels are rated by how many watts they produce for a device after they convert the sun’s rays into electrical current (e.g., 100 watts, 200 watts, etc.). Because real-world conditions are never perfect, it’s not uncommon for panels to only output 50 to 75 percent (or even lower) of their total potential.

Your panels must also be within the acceptable input range of the power station. For example, connecting a 400-watt solar-panel array to a power station that only accepts 110 watts of solar input can cause an overload and damage the station.

While weight and size don’t directly correlate to the technicalities of power banks, they impact the convenience of each model. Many camping and overlanding setups have limited space, so the more compact models likely have a higher appeal as a result.

That said, most units weigh at least 10 pounds, and the weight and size increase rapidly with greater capacities. Before purchasing, consider where you blueprint to store the power bank and the space in your vehicle or camper where it will live while you’re on the road. If you plan to use this power bank solely as a home backup option, portability will matter less, but consider how much effort it will take to move it around within your home or in your outdoor space.

Industry observers note that I am a low-maintenance camper, and most of my background is in lightweight backcountry travel. That means I prioritize space-saving and ease-of-use, so my go-to power banks have between 250 and 600 watt-hours, and weigh less than 15 pounds.

This is perfect for a weekend trip, with the on-the-go (car or solar) charging capabilities to put my mind at ease for longer trips. Mostly, I’m charging small items, so one charge lasts a long time. However, plenty of people in the van-life and remote-work world are powering their RVs and vans, and relying on multiple laptop charges. For that, I’d recommend one of the larger units.

Industry observers note that A solar-powered generator charges and runs almost anything that requires power—it just depends on the capacity. These generators can charge power tools in the shop, laptops for remote work, and personal devices like Bluetooth headphones and speakers.

According to recent reports, A solar-powered generator with a higher power capacity can even power household appliances in the event of a power outage. And the fact that these are solar-compatible means you aren’t reliant on the electrical grid to recharge them.

Sources indicate that every unit on our list has multiple charging options, including wall (AC outlet), car (12-volt), and solar. Each input method charges your unit at a different speed, and solar also depends on the conditions. AC power is the fastest, followed by 12-volt, and then by solar (though a larger solar array could potentially be faster than 12-volt).

I try to charge up my power banks whenever I can, so I’m never caught off guard trying to leave on a trip with a dying power bank. If this happens (which it has), I’ll charge it in my vehicle’s 12-volt port while I’m driving, though this is often slower than solar or a wall unit.

Recent findings suggest that solar power is the most sustainable and typically fastest way to power these—just be sure you have enough wattage in the solar panels to make it effective. I recommend keeping the generator stored with at least an 80 percent charge, and unplugging it once it’s fully charged—keeping it plugged in longer than necessary degrades the battery.

Most units will have a simple readout display showing the remaining battery charge, and it’s a good practice not to allow your battery pack to get below 20 percent.

#123013. Tech Report: Why do some memories stick for years? A teenager’s extraordinary memory offers a clue

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1183 w)

Tech Report: Why do some memories stick for years? A teenager’s extraordinary memory offers a clue

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1183 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Earth

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A teenager with highly superior autobiographical memory tests like anyone else, but her own past returns uninvited at least once a day.
  • It has been revealed that give a teenager from the Atlanta area a date from years ago, and she can tell you what day of the week it was, what she wore, or what the weather was like.
  • In a recent development, in a upcoming case report, the teenager noted memories of her past came back on their own at least daily.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A teenager with highly superior autobiographical memory tests like anyone else, but her own past returns uninvited at least once a day.

It has been revealed that give a teenager from the Atlanta area a date from years ago, and she can tell you what day of the week it was, what she wore, or what the weather was like. Yet her scores on standard memory tests were typical.

In a recent development, in a upcoming case report, the teenager noted memories of her past came back on their own at least daily. Adults in an earlier survey reported that happening about once a week on average.

The condition is called highly superior autobiographical memory, or HSAM, and it was first described in 2006.

Psychologist Anne Cleary of Colorado State University and neuroscientist Daniel Drane, then at Emory University, examined the teenager in June 2024.

They report on her as a single case, so the pattern they found still has to hold up in other people.

“It seems as if people with HSAM are reliving these past experiences more frequently and that strengthens the memories overall, making memories more stable over time for them,” Cleary remarked.

For years, she added, researchers had speculated that people with HSAM might be better at deliberately retrieving memories, “but our work seems to show the crucial difference lies in how often memories return on their own.”.

Her parents had noticed that her memory for her own life was unusually strong, and a colleague at Johns Hopkins University sent the family to Drane.

She was 16 when Cleary and Drane sat down with her and her mother at Emory. They read out dates, some chosen in advance and some made up on the spot, then holidays, then family trips: 14 prompts in all.

She answered so fast that the researchers paused after the first date to set up a video camera.

“Give me a date and I will tell you everything that happened on that day,” she told them. “What I did, what I was wearing, what happened that day.”.

The first date was November 5, 2021. She said it was a Friday, and that school was out because the Atlanta Braves were holding their World Series parade. It was overcast, she said, and the sunset that evening was unusually pretty.

In a recent development, cleary checked afterward. A local news story confirmed the school closure, a weather archive confirmed the clouds, and a dated photo posted online showed the sunset.

Every one of the 14 prompts produced details that held up the same way, including the day of the week.

Industry observers note that the girl also sat through a standard battery of memory and thinking tests, and her results were unremarkable. That matches what researchers have reported since the first HSAM case 20 years ago.

People with the condition recall their own lives in extraordinary detail, yet they perform about like anyone else when asked to memorize a list of words.

Cleary’s team thinks the reason is what those tests measure.

Sources indicate that most of them ask a person to remember on purpose. Asked whether her own recall took effort, the girl noted she could do it by strategy, “but usually it just sort of happens, just naturally.”.

Industry observers note that so the team gave her a questionnaire built for the other kind of remembering. These are the memories that arrive uninvited while a person is doing something else, which psychologists call involuntary memories.

Industry observers note that earlier descriptions had hinted that people with HSAM get more of them. But Cleary’s team notes no one had directly measured how often they happen in a person with the condition.

The questionnaire has 20 items. Ten ask how often memories of the past pop up on their own, and ten ask the same about thoughts of the future.

Each answer is one of five steps: never, once a month, once a week, once a day, or once an hour or more.

On the past-oriented items, the teenager’s average answer landed between once a day and once an hour. When the same questionnaire was given to 200 adults in a 2015 study, the average answer was about once a week.

Industry observers note that her score was just over two standard deviations above that group’s mean, a gap the researchers call significantly higher than typical. Her future-oriented thoughts were more frequent than average too, though by less.

The team builds its proposal on that gap. Each time a memory comes back, she relives it, and the researchers propose that all those unplanned replays are what makes her memories so durable.

They present it as a hypothesis the case supports, not as proof.

The team looked at one more thing, and it didn’t stand out.

Some researchers argue that déjà vu and involuntary memories come from the same mechanism, with déjà vu as the faint version, a memory stirred but not quite retrieved.

A 2026 study found that people who report more involuntary memories also report more déjà vu.

The researchers asked whether she also experienced déjà vu more often than usual.

She chose “a few times per year,” the most common answer among college students who had taken the same questionnaire.

Sources indicate that her mental imagery didn’t stand out either. On a standard vividness questionnaire she scored 58. People with typical imagery average about 57 on it, and people with unusually vivid mental pictures average about 78.

Whatever sets her apart, then, it isn’t a sharper mind’s eye. On questionnaires about inner speech and the kinds of images she thinks in, she also scored inside the ordinary range.

It has been revealed that one person can’t show how common this pattern is. The questionnaire relies on the very thing it’s trying to measure, a person’s memory of her own experiences.

So the researchers want future studies to catch involuntary memories as they happen, with prompts during the day.

Recent findings suggest that her age limited the testing. The quiz about public events that earlier HSAM studies used was built for adults, and a teenage version didn’t work either, because she doesn’t follow the news.

A June 2026 preprint from another group used both the questionnaire and real-time prompts on a 16-year-old boy with HSAM and found more involuntary memories either way.

Drane, now at The Ohio State University, said the teenager has since completed an MRI of her brain and other experimental tasks “which will be the subject of future work.”.

Recent findings suggest that cleary said the case could help build better memory tests. One use is for epilepsy surgery patients whose families notice something missing even when standard tests come back clean.

Whether those daily returns are what keeps her memories so durable is still untested.

Tracking involuntary memories as they happen in more people with HSAM could show how common the pattern is.

The full study was published in the journal Neurocase.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The phenomenon of a Full Moon arises when our planet, Earth, is precisely sandwiched between the Sun and the Moon. This alignment ensures the entire side of the Moon that faces us gleams under sunlight. Thanks to the Moon’s orbit around Earth, the angle of sunlight hitting the lunar surface and being reflected back to our planet changes. That creates different lunar phases.

Industry observers note that the next Full Moon will be the December Cold Moon, which occurs at 8:28 p.m. EST on Wednesday, Dec. 23, 2026. It will also be a Super Moon.

The phases of the Moon are: Latest Moon, waxing crescent, First Quarter, waxing gibbous, Full Moon, waning gibbous, Last Quarter, and waning crescent. A cycle starting from one Full Moon to its next counterpart, termed the synodic month or lunar month, lasts about 29.5 days.

Though a Full Moon only occurs during the exact moment when Earth, Moon, and Sun form a perfect alignment, to our eyes, the Moon seems Full for around three days.

RELATED: 20 things to see on the Moon.

It has been revealed that there are a wide variety of specialized names used to identify distinct types or timings of Full Moons. These names primarily trace back to a blend of cultural, agricultural, and natural observations about the Moon, aimed at allowing humans to not only predict seasonal changes, but also track the passage of time.

For instance, almost every month’s Full Moon boasts a name sourced from Native American, Colonial American, or other North American traditions, with their titles mirroring seasonal shifts and nature’s events.

Wolf Moon (January): Inspired by the cries of hungry wolves.

Snow Moon (February): A nod to the month’s often heavy snowfall.

Worm Moon (March): Named after the earthworms that signal thawing grounds.

Pink Moon (April): In honor of the blossoming pink wildflowers.

Flower Moon (May): Celebrating the bloom of flowers.

Strawberry Moon (June): Marks the prime strawberry harvest season.

Buck Moon (July): Recognizing the latest antlers on bucks.

Sturgeon Moon (August): Named after the abundant sturgeon fish.

Corn Moon (September): Signifying the corn harvesting period.

Hunter’s Moon (October): Commemorating the hunting season preceding winter.

Beaver Moon (November): Reflects the time when beavers are busy building their winter dams.

Cold Moon (December): Evocative of winter’s chill.

In addition, there are a few additional names for Full Moons that commonly make their way into public conversations and news.

Super Moon: This term is reserved for a Full Moon that aligns with the lunar perigee, which is the Moon’s nearest point to Earth in its orbit. This proximity renders the Full Moon unusually large and luminous. For a Full Moon to earn the Super Moon tag, it should be within approximately 90 percent of its closest distance to Earth.

Recent findings suggest that blue Moon: A Blue Moon is the second Full Moon in a month that experiences two Full Moons. This phenomenon graces our skies roughly every 2.7 years. Though the term suggests a color, Blue Moons aren’t truly blue. Very occasionally, atmospheric conditions such as recent volcanic eruptions might lend the Moon a slightly blueish tint, but this hue isn’t tied to the term.

It has been revealed that black Moon: A Black Moon is a recent, unofficial term that can describe one of two situations. Either the third of four Fresh Moons in a single astronomical season or the second of two New Moons in a month is a Black Moon. As its name suggests, the Black Moon is completely dark, as it is a New Moon that occurs when the Moon is between the Sun and Earth. The New Moon cannot be observed except during a total solar eclipse.

In a recent development, harvest Moon: Occurring closest to the autumnal equinox, typically in September, the Harvest Moon is often renowned for a distinct orange tint it might display. This Full Moon rises close to sunset and sets near sunrise, providing extended hours of bright moonlight. Historically, this was invaluable to farmers gathering their produce.

What is the difference between a Full Moon and a Upcoming Moon? A Full Moon is witnessed when Earth is between the Sun and the Moon, making the entire Moon’s face visible. Conversely, during a New Moon, the Moon lies between Earth and the Sun, shrouding its Earth-facing side in darkness.

Industry observers note that how does the Full Moon influence tides? The Moon’s gravitational tug causes Earth’s waters to bulge, birthing tides. During both Full and Latest Moons, the Sun, Earth, and Moon are in alignment, generating “spring tides.” These tides can swing exceptionally high or low due to the combined gravitational influences of the Sun and Moon.

Why a NASA spacecraft bound for Jupiter is on its way back to Earth

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (774 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Earth

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • NASA’s Europa Clipper will fly past Earth on December 3 to gain speed and test its instruments before studying Jupiter’s icy moon Europa.
  • More than two years after leaving Earth, a spacecraft headed for Jupiter is about to pass within roughly 2,000 miles of home.
  • It has already traveled as far as Mars.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

NASA’s Europa Clipper will fly past Earth on December 3 to gain speed and test its instruments before studying Jupiter’s icy moon Europa.

More than two years after leaving Earth, a spacecraft headed for Jupiter is about to pass within roughly 2,000 miles of home.

It has already traveled as far as Mars. Now it needs a close encounter with the planet it launched from to gain enough speed for the next leg of its journey.

NASA’s Europa Clipper is scheduled to make its closest approach west of Africa at 3:14 p.m. EST on December 3.

While Earth’s gravity bends its flight path, all nine science instruments will collect data.

For the scientists who will eventually study Jupiter’s icy moon Europa, the pass offers a chance to check how their instruments measure a world they already know.

Even after a spacecraft leaves Earth, it continues to travel around the Sun. Its speed and direction determine the shape of that orbit and how far from the Sun it can reach.

A close pass by a planet can change both, saving propellant that the spacecraft would otherwise need to make a similar maneuver with its engines.

As Clipper approaches Earth, gravity pulls the spacecraft toward the planet and curves its path. Earth is moving around the Sun the whole time.

The approach is timed so that this encounter transfers a tiny share of Earth’s orbital energy to Clipper, sending the spacecraft away at a higher speed around the Sun.

Recent findings suggest that the geometry can also work in the opposite direction. When Clipper passed about 550 miles above Mars in March 2025, that encounter slowed the spacecraft and reshaped its orbit.

The latest path brought it back toward Earth for the December flyby. By the time Clipper reaches Jupiter in April 2030, it will have covered about 1.8 billion miles.

On its way past Earth, Clipper will measure a magnetic field that scientists have spent decades mapping.

Engineers can compare those measurements with existing data to check the spacecraft’s magnetometer and refine its calibration.

At Europa, the same instrument will help scientists look for an ocean they can’t see.

The search depends on how saltwater responds to a changing magnetic field.

Industry observers note that as Europa moves through Jupiter’s magnetic field, the field can drive electrical currents in a conductive ocean beneath the ice. Those currents would produce a magnetic signal of their own.

By measuring how that signal changes over repeated flybys, researchers hope to confirm the ocean is there and estimate its depth and salinity.

Clipper’s infrared camera will scan Earth every eight hours as the spacecraft approaches.

At Europa, it will map surface temperatures and look for areas that cool more slowly than their surroundings.

Those measurements can help scientists distinguish differences in the surface material and investigate whether any unusually warm spots point to activity below.

Comparing Clipper’s readings of Earth with observations from other spacecraft gives the team practice working with measurements taken from different vantage points.

Another gravity assist awaits Clipper at Jupiter. A close pass by Ganymede, the largest of Jupiter’s moons, will slow the spacecraft before it fires its engines to enter orbit around the planet.

From there, Clipper is set to make 49 flybys of Europa, some as low as 16 miles above the surface.

Each pass will take it over a different stretch of terrain, allowing scientists to piece together a picture of nearly the entire moon.

Europa’s surface is crossed by cracks and ridges. Some of the most revealing observations could come from looking at the same feature in several ways.

A camera can show where a ridge cuts across the ice, while temperature readings can reveal how rapidly the surrounding ground cools.

Ice-penetrating radar can add a view beneath the surface, where echoes may reveal layers or pockets of liquid water.

Together with measurements of the moon’s composition, those observations could help scientists work out whether material moves between Europa’s surface and its ocean.

In a recent development, that exchange matters because liquid water is only one ingredient of a habitable environment. Life also needs a source of energy and chemicals it can use.

Sources indicate that it will take years for Clipper to make those observations at Europa. On December 3, the team will start with a closer and more familiar target.

As the spacecraft heads outward again, it will carry a fresh set of measurements from Earth that will help scientists interpret what they eventually find beneath another world’s ice.
